name: plugin-process-hygiene-convergence
description: Tier-P F1 scenario: an adversarial mock harness validating the transient-hook-client contract (visions/plugin-services 'process-count-scales-with-services-not-sessions' and 'hooks-and-callbacks-are-transient' Behaviors, PR #2300) against a synthetic mock daemon -- NOT a real plugin runtime, so it runs fast, dependency-free (stdlib only), and identically on every OS. Six adversarial scenarios (each a real-OS-process flood, never threads/asyncio): a concurrent flood against a live daemon (all served, exactly one daemon process survives); a flood against an absent daemon (all degrade to inline/no-op, zero self-promoted daemons); a daemon appearing mid-flood (both sides of the transition behave); a daemon dying mid-packet (every in-flight client degrades cleanly within a bounded budget, none hang); a concurrent daemon-election race (exactly one contender wins the single-instance lease, the rest stand down); and a repeated-flood process-count invariant (process count returns to baseline after every round, with zero leftovers). Real per-plugin conformance against this validated contract is issue #2301's own audit, cited against this harness's evidence rather than re-validated here. Design doc: efforts/active/plugin-process-hygiene/adversarial-convergence-mock.md. Name-free / public.
